Terokkar Forest (/ˈtɛ.ɹoʊˌkɑɹ/ TEH-roh-kahr), once known as Talador and the Spires of Arak, is a zone in Outland located east of Nagrand, west of Shadowmoon Valley, southeast of Zangarmarsh, and southwest of Hellfire Peninsula. This forest was most likely named after Terokk, the greatest king in arakkoa history.
Terokkar was seen as the Bone Wastes in previous maps and lore sources, but the Bone Wastes themselves are now a sub-region within the Terokkar Forest zone.

{{Combat}} [[Bleeding Hollow Ruins]] }} [[File:Terokkar.jpg|Terokkar Forest after Talador became corrupted.|thumb]] '''Terokkar Forest''' ({{IPA|/ˈtɛ.ɹoʊˌkɑɹ/}} {{respell|TEH-roh-kahr}}),[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vvrzZgZ2ZDw Blizzard Explains the Entire History of World of Warcraft | WIRED], 14:45 once known as '''[[Talador]]''' and the '''[[Spires of Arak]]''', is a zone in [[Outland]] located east of [[Nagrand]], west of [[Shadowmoon Valley]], southeast of [[Zangarmarsh]], and southwest of [[Hellfire Peninsula]]. This forest was most likely named after [[Terokk]], the greatest king in [[arakkoa]] history. Terokkar was seen as the [[Bone Wastes]] in previous maps and lore sources, but the Bone Wastes themselves are now a sub-region within the Terokkar Forest zone. ==History== Once known as [[Talador]], the region was a forest of red and orange leaved trees that bathed the entire area in a perpetual autumn hue. These beautiful [[olemba tree]]s, and the draenei's equally impressive gardens surrounded the draenei's greatest city on Draenor: Shattrath. A splendorous monument to the skills of the draenei artificers, even in exile, the city's greatness was matched by that of the holy mausoleum Auchindoun, the place where all draenei souls prepared for their journey into the afterlife and where many of their bodies were laid to rest. The smaller city, Tuurem, was just as noteworthy as its more magnificent neighbors, as it sat at a crossroads in the area, and one seeking to travel from Shattrath to Karabor would likely pass through the city. At this time, only the region closest to the [[Spires of Arak]] was known as Terokkar Forest by the [[Arakkoa Outcasts]], and it was under their control.''[[World of Warcraft: Chronicle Volume 2]]'', pg. 46 When the Orcish Horde rampaged across Draenor, Talador was rendered the draenei's final stronghold. The Orcish Horde were repelled from Talador for a time, but when they imbibed the Blood of Mannoroth, the demonic fury they were granted gave them the power they needed to cut through to the city of Shattrath itself. Their fel magic corrupted the region, turning the red and orange trees a pale, dusky green that transformed the forest into a dark, eerie woodland. The siege of Shattrath ultimately left the city in ruins and the draenei scattered and presumed extinct by the orcs and their Burning Legion masters. Once the majority of the Orcish Horde departed for Azeroth, all of Talador came under the dominion of the Arakkoa Outcasts, and the region was renamed Terokkar in honor of [[Terokk]], their lost king. At a later point, the orcs who had conquered Auchindoun performed a ritual that destroyed the building and much of the surrounding area, creating the [[Bone Wastes]]. ==Geography== The flora consists mostly of dark green forest vegetation of crystal pines known as [[olemba tree]]s. [[Shattrath City]] lies in the northwestern portion of the zone. Alliance and Horde each have a town.
The multi-winged instance [[Auchindoun]] can be found in this zone, containing four separate 5-man dungeons. There are no raid dungeons, micro dungeons, battlegrounds, or arenas in this zone. The spirit towers of the [[Bone Wastes]] provide a world PvP opportunity. Every so often you can hear a roar while near Auchindoun - this is [[Teribus the Cursed]], flying in circles around Auchindoun. ===Maps and subregions=== [[File:VZ-Terokkar Forest.jpg|thumb|left|Map of Terokkar Forest.]] {| class="darktable hlist" |- | *[[Allerian Post]] *[[Allerian Stronghold]] *[[Auchindoun]] **[[Auchenai Crypts]] **[[Mana-Tombs]] **[[Ring of Observance]] **[[Sethekk Halls]] **[[Shadow Labyrinth]] **[[Shadow Stair|The Shadow Stair]] *[[Barrier Hills|The Barrier Hills]] *[[Bleeding Hollow Ruins]] *[[Bonechewer Ruins]] *[[Bone Wastes|The Bone Wastes]] **[[Auchenai Grounds]] **[[Carrion Hill]] **[[Derelict Caravan]] **[[Refugee Caravan]] **[[Sha'tari Base Camp]] **[[Shadow Tomb]] **[[Tomb of Lights]] **[[Writhing Mound]] *[[Cenarion Thicket]] *[[Firewing Point]] *[[Grangol'var Village]] *[[Lake Ere'Noru]] *[[Lake Jorune]] *[[Netherweb Ridge]] *[[Raastok Glade]] *[[Razorthorn Rise]] *[[Razorthorn Shelf]] *[[Shattrath City]] *[[Silmyr Lake]] *[[Skethyl Mountains]] **[[Blackwind Landing]] **[[Blackwind Valley]] **[[Skettis]] ***[[Blackwind Lake]] ***[[Lower Veil Shil'ak]] ***[[Upper Veil Shil'ak]] ***[[Veil Ala'rak]] ***[[Veil Harr'ik]] ***[[Terokk's Rest]] *[[Stonebreaker Camp]] *[[Stonebreaker Hold]] *[[Sorrow Wing Point]] *[[Tuurem]] *[[Veil Lithic]] *[[Veil Reskk]] *[[Veil Rhaze]] *[[Veil Shalas]] *[[Veil Shienor]] *[[Veil Skith]] *[[Wayne's Refuge]] |- || ---- ;Removed locations *[[Broken Hills|The Broken Hills]] *[[Misty Ridge]] *[[Olembas]] *[[Sha'tari Outpost]] |- | ---- ;[[Lore location]]s *[[Telmor]] |- | ---- ;{{WC2-inline}} [[Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal|Warcraft II]] *[[Fortress Auchindoun]] |} {{clear|left}} ===Instances=== [[File:TerokkarConcept.jpg|thumb|Concept art.]] [[File:Terokkar Forest.jpg|thumb|In-game.]] {| class="darktable" ! The novel ''[[Beyond the Dark Portal]]'' stated an explosion during the war against the draenei, while ingame text[[The Codex of Blood (quest)]][[Into the Heart of the Labyrinth]] said the explosion occurred two years before the events of ''[[World of Warcraft: The Burning Crusade]]''. *The {{Expac|The Burning Crusade}} Flash site had this to say about the zone: "New hope has come to this ancient forest. Aided by the benevolent [[naaru]], a group of [[draenei]] has rebuilt [[Shattrath City]]. The city has since thrown open its doors to welcome refugees of many different races from all over Outland. Yet the past has not left this area unmarked.
